key_insight: SLiR turns activation-function relaxation into a general, optimizable shifting procedure, replacing hand-crafted bounds with a scalable method for many nonlinearities.
engineering_relevance: This makes neural network verification easier to extend to new activations while preserving soundness and improving practical solvability in safety-critical systems.
method: Parameterize each relaxation by its slope.
Compute the offset with a shifting procedure that enforces valid upper and lower bounds over the input domain.
Use only a Lipschitz constant or critical points, making the method broadly applicable.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tight relaxations across a wide range of practical activation functions and up to 7.8× more verified properties than state-of-the-art methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on choosing appropriate slopes and on having reliable Lipschitz constants or critical points; poor estimates may weaken bounds or optimization quality.
paper_title: Shifting-based Optimizable Linear Relaxations for General Activation Functions
